open_points.subject: FlowVersion content identity
open_points.text: “Lists whose order carries no meaning are sorted before hashing — … edges in the edge order of A05, constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`) — so the same content in another order has the same identity”
open_points.question: How are edges or constants ordered for hashing when two entries have the same stated sort key but differ in guard or value, given that such duplicate-target structures may be kept as unproven versions?
options: Extend the sort key with every meaning fact
Preserve submitted order for equal keys
Reject equal sort keys during composition
open_points.default_guess: Extend the sort key with the canonical JSON of all remaining meaning facts.

open_points.subject: FlowNode identifiers and flow endpoints
open_points.text: “A flow input or flow output endpoint has the empty string as its node”
open_points.question: Must `node_id` be non-empty, or may a real node use the empty string reserved for ordering flow endpoints?
options: Refuse an empty `node_id`
Allow it and distinguish endpoints structurally
Reserve a different endpoint marker
open_points.default_guess: Refuse an empty `node_id`.

open_points.subject: Guard-disabled nodes
open_points.text: M15 says “A node whose every incoming edge is disabled by its guard is not executed”; A13 says “An input port that can no longer receive a value because every edge into it is disabled … makes its node `skipped_by_guard`”
open_points.question: Is a node skipped when any required input becomes unreachable, or only when all incoming edges of the node are disabled?
options: Skip when any input port cannot receive a value
Skip only when every incoming edge of the node is disabled
open_points.default_guess: Skip when any required input port can no longer receive a value.

open_points.subject: Guard value comparison
open_points.text: “A guarded edge delivers only when its guard port's value equals its guard value.”
open_points.question: What equality relation is used for JSON guard values, especially numbers such as `1` and `1.0` and composite enum values?
options: Equality of canonical JSON bytes
JSON data-model equality
Host-language equality
open_points.default_guess: Use equality of canonical JSON bytes.

open_points.subject: Disclosure propagation through alternative inputs
open_points.text: “for a function node, the highest class that can reach any of its inputs”
open_points.question: When mutually exclusive guarded edges can reach the same input, is the proof-time class the maximum over every possible edge, only simultaneously deliverable edges, or guard-specific?
options: Maximum over every possible source edge
Compute a separate class for each guard outcome
Ignore sources that cannot deliver simultaneously
open_points.default_guess: Take the maximum over every source that can deliver under any guard outcome.

open_points.subject: Function filesystem access
open_points.text: K-02 says a function has “no filesystem beyond its input”; A03 permits opening paths “inside the exchange directory and the read-only runtime”
open_points.question: May agent code read arbitrary runtime and exchange-directory files, or must it be restricted to its declared inputs despite the runner itself needing those paths?
options: Agent code may read the permitted directories
Agent code may read only declared input files while runner internals have broader access
Any filesystem open by agent code is a sandbox violation
open_points.default_guess: Restrict agent code to declared inputs while granting runner internals the access they need.

open_points.subject: Function purity and deterministic admission
open_points.text: “Admission is a deterministic verdict” and “no clock, no randomness”, while A03 traps only the listed entry points
open_points.question: What happens when code observes an untrapped nondeterministic source such as process identity, resource counters, runtime-file metadata, locale or another standard-library clock/entropy path?
options: Such access is forbidden and must be trapped
It is allowed, so determinism is not guaranteed
Admission must repeat executions and detect differing output
open_points.default_guess: Treat every observable nondeterministic source as forbidden and classify a recorded access as `sandbox_violation`.

open_points.subject: Sandbox scratch ceiling
open_points.text: “one private exchange directory bounded by `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`”
open_points.question: Which bytes count toward the scratch ceiling—staged code, input values and files, runner files, temporary files, and outputs—and what outcome occurs if the directory is already over the ceiling before `run` starts?
options: Count all bytes in the exchange directory
Count only bytes created or returned by agent code
Count inputs and outputs but exclude runner and code files
open_points.default_guess: Count all exchange-directory bytes attributable to the execution and return `resource_exhausted` if staging or execution exceeds the ceiling.

open_points.subject: Sandbox cleanup failure
open_points.text: A03 rule 5 says the first of timeout, resource exhaustion, sandbox violation, crash and contract violation decides; rule 7 says unconfirmed cleanup makes the execution `crashed` with `cleanup_failed`
open_points.question: If an execution first times out, exhausts a limit or triggers a sandbox trap and cleanup then cannot be confirmed, which outcome is recorded?
options: Always override with `crashed/cleanup_failed`
Keep the earlier outcome and separately record cleanup failure
Apply rule 5 and ignore cleanup failure in the execution outcome
open_points.default_guess: Override with `crashed` and detail `cleanup_failed`, because rule 7 explicitly discards the output and stops the kernel.

open_points.subject: Trial-case validation
open_points.text: A04 first orders “input values fit … expected outputs … every value is within” the size limits, then says ports are checked by “presence, carriage, schema, then size”
open_points.question: Is validation performed category-wide—every input schema before any expected-output or size check—or port-by-port with each port's size checked before moving to the next category?
options: Top-level category order first
Port-by-port order including size
Inputs port-by-port, then expected outputs port-by-port
open_points.default_guess: Validate all input ports port-by-port, then all expected-output ports port-by-port, using presence, carriage, schema and size for each.

open_points.subject: Rollback target
open_points.text: “Rollback activates an earlier implementation of the slot's current contract version”
open_points.question: Does “earlier” mean submitted before the current implementation, previously activated before it, or simply any non-current implementation with a current-corpus admitted verdict?
options: Any non-current admitted implementation
Only one submitted before the current implementation
Only one appearing in an earlier activation
open_points.default_guess: Allow any non-current implementation admitted over the current corpus.

open_points.subject: Manifest revision access
open_points.text: “The kernel reads a service's record only from `<manifest_location>/<service_id>.json` at the configured `manifest_revision`”
open_points.question: How is a file at a repository revision actually obtained, and what exact failure is produced when the location is not a repository, the revision is absent, or the path is absent at that revision?
options: Read through a version-control object API without checkout
Require `manifest_location` to be a checkout already fixed at that revision
Have the installer materialize the selected revision
open_points.default_guess: Read the blob directly from the version-control object database at the configured revision and treat any lookup failure as manifest mismatch.

open_points.subject: Binding port schemas
open_points.text: A08 refuses ports that “break a rule A02 sets for contract ports — unique names per direction, a media type exactly on `file` ports” but does not name A02's supported-schema check
open_points.question: Must every binding port's `value_schema` be in the kernel's supported JSON Schema subset?
options: Apply the supported-schema restriction to bindings
Allow any JSON Schema in bindings
Apply only the two port rules explicitly repeated by A08
open_points.default_guess: Require binding schemas to use the same supported subset as contract schemas.

open_points.subject: Binding acceptance after manifest change
open_points.text: A08 rule 7 re-runs rule 5 and says refusal uses `binding_stale` “when only the digest differs”
open_points.question: Where in the ordered acceptance checks is comparison of the current operation digest with the proposal's pinned digest performed, especially when the digest and another manifest or instance check both fail?
options: Compare immediately after locating and validating the capability entry
Compare after every rule 5 check
Report `binding_stale` only if every other check passes
open_points.default_guess: Run the ordered rule 5 checks first and compare the digest last, so `binding_stale` is used only when it is the sole remaining failure.

open_points.subject: Manifest idempotency_key value
open_points.text: “`null` means none; otherwise the text split on `+`” and for reads the binding copies the split text “whatever those parts are”
open_points.question: What happens when `idempotency_key` is missing or is a non-null, non-string JSON value, particularly for a `read` operation whose key syntax is otherwise not checked?
options: Treat missing as `null` and refuse non-string values
Require the member and allow only null or string
Ignore any value for reads
open_points.default_guess: Require the member to be either null or a string; treat a missing or other-typed value as manifest mismatch.

open_points.subject: Instance base URL
open_points.text: A08 requires “an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host”; A09 appends the declared path after removing a trailing slash
open_points.question: Are user information, query, fragment, non-root base paths, percent escapes and other components allowed in `api_base_url`, and exactly how are they combined with the operation path?
options: Allow only scheme, authority and an optional path prefix
Allow only scheme and authority
Allow every absolute HTTP URL and apply a specified URL-resolution algorithm
open_points.default_guess: Allow scheme, authority and an optional path prefix, but refuse user information, query and fragment; append the operation path to the prefix without normalization.

open_points.subject: Host header and request identity
open_points.text: “`host` — the authority of `api_base_url` exactly as the manifest writes it, not normalized”
open_points.question: How is the authority extracted and serialized when the URL uses host case differences, an explicit default port, IPv6 notation, percent encoding or user information?
options: Use the literal authority substring from the manifest
Parse and serialize a normalized host and port
Refuse forms that do not have one canonical literal authority
open_points.default_guess: Use the literal host-and-port authority substring, while refusing user information and ambiguous URL forms.

open_points.subject: Multipart request framing
open_points.text: The approval description excludes the multipart boundary because it is “the kernel's framing”
open_points.question: How is a multipart boundary chosen and checked so that it cannot collide with arbitrary file or value content, and what happens if no permitted boundary is collision-free?
options: Generate a boundary and scan all parts for collision
Use a deterministic content-derived boundary with collision extension
Rely on the HTTP library's random boundary without collision checking
open_points.default_guess: Derive a deterministic boundary from the part descriptions and extend it until scanning confirms it does not occur in any encoded part.

open_points.subject: HTTP response status classification
open_points.text: A09's outcome table covers only `1xx`, `2xx`, `3xx`, `4xx` and `5xx`
open_points.question: How is a syntactically three-digit status outside 100–599 classified?
options: Treat it as a malformed response
Treat 600–999 like `5xx`
Use the leading digit regardless of range
open_points.default_guess: Treat any status outside 100–599 as a malformed response: `service_unreachable` for reads and `outcome_unknown` for other operations.

open_points.subject: HTTP response body transport failures
open_points.text: “request may have been sent, no valid final response received” lists timeout, reset, EOF and malformed status or headers, while the 2xx rules assume a body is available
open_points.question: How are malformed chunk framing, invalid transfer encoding, a truncated `Content-Length` body, or a timeout/reset after valid final headers but before the body completes classified?
options: No valid final response: unreachable/unknown
A 2xx contract violation with a non-read attempt marked applied
Classify by status if received, regardless of body transport failure
open_points.default_guess: Treat an incomplete or malformed body as no valid final response: `service_unreachable` for reads and `outcome_unknown` for non-read operations.

open_points.subject: StandingGrant target
open_points.text: “A grant is given only for a node of the flow's active version whose effect class is not `destructive`”
open_points.question: What happens when the named node is a function node and therefore has no effect class?
options: Refuse because only operation nodes can be granted
Allow a permanently unused grant
Treat the absent class as `read`
open_points.default_guess: Refuse grants for function nodes.

open_points.subject: Configuration token reload
open_points.text: “when they differ, or the file cannot be read, it re-reads it” and “When any fails, every request is refused … until a re-read passes”
open_points.question: After a failed re-read, which digest is remembered and what causes later requests to retry if the invalid file's bytes have not changed?
options: Retry parsing and validation on every request until valid
Remember the invalid digest and retry only after bytes change
Keep the last valid digest but no usable token list
open_points.default_guess: Enter an invalid-configuration state and retry the complete read and validation on every request until it succeeds.

open_points.subject: Configuration replacement after startup
open_points.text: A17 requires the configuration to be a regular, owner-only, non-symlink file, while A16 says token-list re-reads apply exactly four checks and “Every other … start check applies only at a restart”
open_points.question: May the live configuration path be replaced after startup by a symlink or insecurely owned or permissioned file whose token list is then accepted?
options: Recheck file type, ownership, permissions and no-follow on every token reload
Apply those checks only at startup and accept later replacements
Refuse all live token-list changes and require restart
open_points.default_guess: Open without following symlinks and recheck regular-file ownership and permissions on every reload.

open_points.subject: Configuration reload snapshot
open_points.text: “reads the configuration file and compares the SHA-256 of its bytes with that of the last read; when they differ … it re-reads it”
open_points.question: Must hashing, parsing and token replacement use one immutable read of the same file bytes, or may the file change between comparison and parsing?
options: Use one opened-file snapshot for hash and parse
Read twice and verify both hashes match
Permit separate reads
open_points.default_guess: Read once from a safely opened file and use those exact bytes for both hashing and parsing.

open_points.subject: Release ceiling changes and existing data
open_points.text: “A new release may change ceilings. They bind contract versions issued after it; a contract version issued earlier keeps its bounds”
open_points.question: What happens to existing implementations, StoredValues, trial fixtures and other durable records that exceed a newly lowered non-contract ceiling?
options: Grandfather every existing durable object
Refuse startup until oversized objects are migrated
Keep objects readable but refuse their future execution or reuse under the new ceiling
open_points.default_guess: Grandfather existing durable objects for reading and for executions already defined by existing contracts, while applying new ceilings only to newly accepted objects.

open_points.subject: Store crash guarantees
open_points.text: “Every change is … one transaction” and “a completed file a record names is never overwritten”
open_points.question: Which SQLite journal, synchronization and file/directory flush guarantees are required so a power loss cannot leave a committed record naming an unpublished file or lose a supposedly committed state transition?
options: Require fully durable SQLite and fsync ordering for files, directories and commits
Guarantee only process-crash atomicity, not power-loss durability
Permit platform-default SQLite durability
open_points.default_guess: Require a durable journal mode and explicit ordering: publish and fsync data plus its directory before committing a referencing database transaction, then durably commit the transaction.
